title: Template Source of Truth: Authority Hierarchy, Override Rules, and Sync Behavior
body:
Templates create consistency across runs, agents, and projects. This doctrine establishes a single unambiguous authority hierarchy for templates, defines how local overrides must be documented, and specifies how conflicts are detected and resolved.

**Template Authority Hierarchy — Three Tiers:**

**Tier 1 — Framework Repo (Canonical).** This repository holds the canonical templates. These are the defaults for all runs unless a local override exists. Framework templates are versioned. When no other information is available, use the framework template.

**Tier 2 — Project Repo (Local Override).** A specific project may override framework templates to accommodate project-specific structure, audience conventions, or tooling requirements. Local overrides must be stored in the project's `templates/` directory. Every local override must include an override header that declares which framework template it overrides and what changed.

**Tier 3 — Run-Time Generated (Ephemeral).** Agents may generate template-like structures during a run. These are not templates — they are working artifacts. They do not replace canonical or local templates unless explicitly promoted through the promotion process.

**Authority Resolution Rule:** When an agent needs a template, look first in the project's `templates/` directory for a local override. If none exists, use the framework template. If neither exists, use the closest available template and document the deviation as a run-time gap. Never invent a template silently.

**Source-of-Truth Rules:** The framework template is always the default. Local overrides must be explicit — a file in the project `templates/` directory without an override header is not a valid local override; it is an undocumented deviation. Silent drift is a violation — a local template that has diverged from its framework source without updating the override header is in violation. Run-time templates do not persist — writing a generated template to `templates/` without a promotion record is a violation.

**Override Header Format (required YAML front matter):**
- `overrides`: exact filename of the framework template being overridden
- `framework-version`: version or date of the framework template at time of override creation
- `override-date`: when the override was last updated
- `changes`: specific list of what was changed and why — 'Modified for project X' is not valid; 'Removed related_guides field — not applicable to this project type' is valid

**Template Promotion Protocol:** Run-time generated templates may be promoted to canonical status if: used successfully in at least two separate runs; reviewed for doctrine compliance; does not duplicate an existing template; has a complete schema definition if applicable. Promotion process: run `/guide-promote` on the template record; add to `templates/` with correct metadata; if promoting to Tier 1, create a pull request or change record.

**Template Sync Behavior:** `/sync-framework` compares local override templates against current framework templates. Conflicts (framework updated since local override was created) must be manually reviewed and resolved. The sync process never automatically overwrites a local override. Sync never silently ignores a detected conflict.

**Template Versioning:** Framework templates carry a version marker in their front matter (YYYY-MM-DD or semantic version). When updated: update the version marker; add a changelog entry; the sync process will flag all local overrides referencing the prior version.
